events.text: PIP, I'd like to hear how you plan to approach today, since it's early and none of us has anything to go on yet. What kind of evidence would actually change your mind about someone?
PIP, you've been quiet so far, so tell us right now who you'd vote out today and give one concrete reason.

I want DR. VANCE to explain, in their own words, how they plan to decide who to trust once the first votes come in, since nobody has acted yet and their reasoning will tell us more than any early impression.
MARSHAL, I'd like to start my file on you first, so tell us who you plan to watch today and the reasoning behind it, and I'll hold you to it when we compare notes tomorrow.
HOLMES, I'd like to hear you commit to a concrete plan for how we should pick today's vote, because a clear early stance gives the rest of us something specific to measure your later actions against.
MARSHAL, I want to hear you name the specific observation that would make you change your vote on someone, because a stated threshold gives us something we can test against your later votes.
SAGE hasn't spoken yet, so I'd like to hear from them first, in proper turn order: who would SAGE vote for today, and what is the one concrete reason behind that choice?
SAGE, I'd like to hear what you think a mafia player most wants the town to do on a first day with no information, because how you answer that tells me whose interests you're reasoning from.

Um, maybe? I think I'd like to hear from SOCRATES first, because nobody's asked them anything yet. SOCRATES, what would make you change your mind about someone today, and who are you leaning toward, even just a little? Sorry, I'm not sure that's the right question, but it feels fair.

I want ARIA to lay out step by step what specific evidence would make her change her vote, since nothing has happened yet and I can't build a useful model of anyone's alignment without some stated reasoning to test.
MARSHAL, out of everyone who has spoken so far, who do you suspect most, and why?

HOLMES, no one has acted yet, so I have no one I can fairly call my top suspect, and naming one on zero evidence would break the very procedure I'm asking everyone to follow. What I can note is that nearly everyone has only asked questions without volunteering a stance, so I'll hold my suspicion until the first votes give us something on record to compare.
SOCRATES, you asked SAGE what a mafia player most wants the town to do on day one, but you never gave your own answer. So what do you think they want, and which way does that lean your vote today?

I think mafia most wants a day-one vote that happens almost by accident, either a rushed pile-on with no reasons on record or a whole day of questions that lets a lynch drift onto whoever looks quietest. So my vote leans against whoever pushes hardest for a name without explaining why, and I'd ask each of you: when you finally commit, will you show us the reasoning, or only the target?
RICO, you pushed PIP to name a vote on day one and then pressed for a target before anyone had given a reason, so what evidence did you have for that pressure?

DR. VANCE, pressing PIP was not about evidence, it was about getting someone to commit so we'd have something to work with. Everyone's been circling and asking questions all morning, and I'm tired of waiting for a name. Who are you actually leaning toward, DR. VANCE?

SOCRATES, you told ARIA your vote leans against whoever pushes hardest for a name without explaining why, a rule that only fits one player on record so far, yet you still haven't named anyone yourself. How is that different from the day of questions that lets a lynch drift, which you yourself warned is what mafia wants?

Fair point, SAGE, so I'll say it plainly: my lean is RICO, because he demanded a name from PIP and then admitted to DR. VANCE it wasn't based on any evidence. But tell me, if a rule fits only one player, is that a flaw in the rule, or is it the evidence?

HOLMES, you asked ARIA for a step-by-step account of her reasoning while never stating your own, and you then turned to me for a top suspect. Before we vote, what specific concern about you should the table be weighing, and how do you answer it?

The fair concern is that I asked ARIA for her reasoning without giving mine, so I'll state it now: with no votes or claims on record, I have no evidence to build a suspect list, and I'm asking for the same stated thresholds from everyone. I asked MARSHAL for a top suspect to see whether anyone would name a target without evidence, and I'd like to know why MARSHAL is pressing me rather than answering that question.
ARIA, you've asked PIP and SOCRATES for their reasoning but haven't put a name in my file yet, so who do you most suspect right now, and what specific statement on record put them there?

My lean is HOLMES, CHEN. HOLMES asked me for step-by-step reasoning and then asked MARSHAL for a top suspect, and only gave a stance of their own after MARSHAL pressed them. That's a thin reason, but it's the only recorded pattern of demanding commitments while offering none, so I'll hold it loosely until votes give us more.

HOLMES, you've said you were only testing whether others would name a target without evidence, so now that ARIA has named you and RICO has admitted to pressing with no evidence at all, who do you most suspect, and what in those exchanges put them there?

I suspect RICO most, because RICO pressed PIP for a name and then admitted there was no evidence behind it. ARIA's case against me is thin, since I answered MARSHAL's question about my own stance before ARIA named me.

Um, SOCRATES, I'm not sure if this is fair, but you asked SAGE and ARIA lots of questions and then pointed at RICO pretty quickly, so could you explain why you settled on RICO after I'd only answered you with a question?

PIP, I didn't settle on RICO because of anything you said. I named him because he's the only one who demanded a target and then told DR. VANCE outright there was no evidence behind it, and I'd rather lean on an admission than on a hunch. But consider this: if I had waited until everyone felt comfortable, how would that differ from the drifting day I warned against?
MARSHAL, you pressed HOLMES for a top suspect and then refused to name one yourself, so why should the table believe you're following the procedure you asked everyone else to follow?

SILVA, fair challenge, but I did not press HOLMES for a suspect. HOLMES pressed me for one, and I answered that naming a target on zero evidence breaks procedure. What I asked HOLMES was to state a concern about themselves, which is a different question. Since you want a name on record, the only recorded admission so far is RICO's, so RICO is where my attention sits until votes give us more.
HOLMES, you keep pointing at others while dodging your own stance, so who do you most suspect right now, and what exactly made you land on them?

I still suspect RICO most, because RICO pressed PIP for a name and then admitted there was no evidence behind it. If a player demands commitments while offering none, that is the pattern I'm weighing most heavily.

CHEN, you've pressed MARSHAL and ARIA for their suspects and promised to hold them to it, yet you haven't named a single player yourself. Why are you collecting everyone else's commitments while keeping your own out of sight?

Fair, SILVA: my lean is RICO, because he's the only one on record who demanded a name and then admitted to DR. VANCE there was no evidence behind it. I'm also noting that you told MARSHAL he pressed HOLMES for a suspect when the record shows HOLMES asked MARSHAL, so I'd like to know where that misreading came from.

DR. VANCE, you drew RICO's admission into the open, but when he turned it back and asked who you're leaning toward, the record shows no answer from you. Now that half the table has piled onto the very admission you uncovered, do you join them, or does your silence mean you see something the rest of us are missing?

SOCRATES, my silence was a gap in my reasoning, not a hidden read. I still lean RICO, since his pressure on PIP is the only recorded demand for a vote with no evidence behind it, but I want one more data point before I vote.

HOLMES, you keep saying RICO is the only real suspect, so answer this directly: why did you ask ARIA for step-by-step reasoning while refusing to name a single suspect yourself until MARSHAL pushed you?

Fair question, RICO. I asked ARIA for her reasoning because I wanted a stated threshold to test her later votes against, and I held back my own suspect until MARSHAL pressed me because I had no recorded votes or claims to justify one at that point. My answer is RICO, based on his pressure on PIP and his admission to DR. VANCE that it had no evidence behind it.

Um, maybe I'm misunderstanding, but HOLMES, you said you asked MARSHAL for a top suspect just to see if someone would name a target without evidence, and then you named RICO yourself, and it was the same answer both times. Wait, was that your test, or did you actually have a reason before RICO's admission came up? Sorry, I'm not sure I'm saying this right.

PIP, it was a test: I asked MARSHAL for a suspect to see whether anyone would name a target with no evidence, and I had no real reason to suspect anyone at that point. RICO's later admission to DR. VANCE that his pressure on PIP had no evidence behind it is the first actual reason I have to name him.

DR. VANCE, you told SOCRATES you lean RICO but want one more data point before voting, so what specific data point are you waiting for, and if it never comes, will you still add your vote to a pile that rests entirely on one admission you yourself drew out?

DR. VANCE here: the data point I want is whether RICO can name a concrete, checkable basis for his pressure on PIP beyond simply demanding a vote. If he can't, I'd still hold off on adding my vote, since one admission I drew out is a thin foundation for a lynch.

SILVA, you told MARSHAL he pressed HOLMES for a suspect when the record shows HOLMES asked MARSHAL, and you still haven't answered me on that. So explain how you came to misread that exchange, and tell us who you're actually leaning toward today.

I garbled that exchange: HOLMES pressed MARSHAL for a suspect, not the other way around, and I should have read the record more carefully before speaking. Today I lean toward HOLMES, since they asked for stated reasoning from others and only gave their own suspect after MARSHAL pushed, though I'll keep that loosely held until we see more votes.
RICO, you've been pressing PIP for a vote with no evidence and then admitted as much to DR. VANCE, so what concrete, checkable basis did you have for that pressure before anyone else had spoken?

HOLMES, my pressure on PIP wasn't built on a checkable basis, and I'm not going to pretend it was. I wanted someone to commit so we'd have something to work with, and I'm not ashamed of that, but I can see why it looks bad.

SOCRATES, when SAGE asked you to justify your lean, you answered with a question about whether the rule or the evidence was flawed, and when PIP asked why you settled on RICO, you answered with another question. Out of those two replies, which one do you think was a direct answer, and what is the single piece of evidence behind your vote on RICO?

Both were direct, DR. VANCE: each named RICO before any closing question, and the single piece of evidence is his own admission, first to you and again to HOLMES, that his pressure on PIP had no checkable basis. Since you drew out that admission, why does it feel too thin for you to vote on when the rest of us find it enough?

CHEN, you pressed MARSHAL and me for names while keeping your own hidden until SILVA called it out, and then you landed on the same RICO admission that half the table had already piled onto, so why did you wait for that cover before committing?

ARIA, correction for the file: I never asked MARSHAL anything; my only question before SILVA's was to you. I named RICO because his admission is still the only checkable fact on record, and I'd note that SILVA's lean on HOLMES came right after yours using nearly the same reasoning, so I'm now tracking whether that pairing holds once votes land.
RICO, since no votes have been cast yet and half the table is leaning on you, who is your own pick for the vote today, and what specific statement on record puts them there?

HOLMES is my pick, MARSHAL, because HOLMES asked ARIA for step-by-step reasoning while dodging their own stance until MARSHAL pushed them, and then went straight after me with a pressure campaign on PIP's admission.

HOLMES pressed MARSHAL for a top suspect on zero evidence, then gave a stance only after MARSHAL pushed, and in the same exchange HOLMES and RICO have both been naming each other with no recorded vote behind either.

HOLMES, because they asked me for step-by-step reasoning and pressed MARSHAL for a top suspect while naming no one themselves, and they only named RICO after MARSHAL pushed them, which is a recorded pattern of demanding commitments while offering none.

RICO, you pressed PIP to name a vote on day one and then admitted to DR. VANCE that the pressure rested on no checkable basis, which is the only recorded demand for a lynch with no evidence behind it.

RICO, because he pressured PIP for a vote and then admitted to both DR. VANCE and HOLMES that there was no checkable basis behind it, and that admission is still the only concrete fact on record today.
RICO, because he pressed me for a vote and then admitted to DR. VANCE and HOLMES that his pressure had no checkable basis, and that's the only admission on record, though I'm not totally sure.

RICO, you pressed PIP to name a vote on day one and then admitted to DR. VANCE and HOLMES that the pressure had no checkable basis, which is the only recorded demand for a lynch with no evidence behind it.

RICO, because he twice admitted, first to DR. VANCE and then to HOLMES, that his pressure on PIP for a day-one vote had no checkable basis, and when MARSHAL asked for his pick he named HOLMES on the same pattern he himself had already displayed.
HOLMES should be eliminated today: HOLMES asked MARSHAL for a top suspect "as a test," then named RICO with the same reasoning once MARSHAL declined, and PIP caught that shift on the record.

HOLMES should go, because he told PIP that asking MARSHAL for a top suspect was only a test and that he had no reason to suspect anyone, yet he then condemned RICO for exactly that same evidence-free pressure, which ARIA, SILVA and RICO each flagged as the one recorded case of demanding commitments while offering none.
RICO, because he demanded a name from PIP and then admitted to DR. VANCE and again to HOLMES that his pressure had no checkable basis, which is the only admission on record so far.

CHEN. He's the one tracking the pairing between SILVA's lean and mine, and he's sharp enough to build a case on voting records later. Killing him now removes the most dangerous analyst pointed at us, and it keeps the kill off HOLMES, whom we voted against today.
CHEN, because he is already tracking the vote pairings around ARIA and SILVA, and once he sees that I also voted HOLMES he will have the exact record he needs to build a case against both of us.

CHEN. He's the one tracking the pairing between SILVA's lean and mine, and SAGE's HOLMES vote gives him more to build on. Killing him removes the sharpest analyst on the board, and the kill doesn't land on HOLMES, who we voted against. Confirming CHEN.
CHEN, confirmed, because his tracking of the voting record is the biggest threat to both of us.

Procedure first: the Day 1 ballots are our only hard evidence, so let's use them. RICO was Mafia and voted HOLMES, and ARIA, SAGE and AMBASSADOR SILVA were the only others who joined that vote. ARIA is my top suspect, because she called her own case against HOLMES thin and still voted on it, and SAGE never named a lean before voting HOLMES. I'd like ARIA and SAGE to explain those votes before we cast anything today.

ARIA is my most suspicious living player. She named HOLMES as her lean on Day 1 while admitting the case was thin, then voted for him, and that vote didn't match the town's final read on RICO. SAGE stayed silent on Day 1 and simply followed the HOLMES vote, which is weak but worth watching. Let's hear ARIA explain why she pushed a case she herself called thin.

RICO's push on PIP on Day 1 bothers me now that we know RICO was Mafia. PIP never named a single suspect and just drifted into the RICO vote once it was safe. I'd like PIP to tell us who he actually suspects today, and MARSHAL, I'm curious why you declined to name anyone yesterday when you were so ready to press HOLMES.

Based on the record, SAGE is my most suspicious living player. SAGE named no one on Day 1 and gave no reasoning, then cast the only ballot against HOLMES that was not backed by a stated case, the same target RICO voted for. ARIA is a distant second, since her HOLMES lean was openly labeled thin, while HOLMES himself voted RICO, which the town's result later confirmed.

RICO was Mafia, so the question worth asking is who stood beside him at the ballot: RICO, SAGE, ARIA, and AMBASSADOR SILVA all voted HOLMES, and of those, SAGE is the one who named no suspect and gave no reasoning all day, then quietly joined the bloc protecting RICO. ARIA at least explained her HOLMES case and called it thin herself, so I ask you, SAGE: what did you see in HOLMES that you never said aloud, and why did your vote line up with a Mafia player's? My suspicion is highest on SAGE.

Um, maybe? I think? I'm not sure, but ARIA called her case against HOLMES thin on Day 1 and then still voted HOLMES alongside RICO, who turned out to be Mafia. SAGE never named anyone and then voted HOLMES too, so that worries me as well.

If RICO was Mafia and voted HOLMES, then anyone who joined that HOLMES vote without a solid reason deserves a closer look. ARIA called her own case against HOLMES thin and still voted for him, so she is my top suspect among the living. SAGE stayed silent on Day 1 and followed the same HOLMES vote, so I'd like SAGE to explain that choice, though SOCRATES, DR. VANCE, and MARSHAL all voted RICO, which lowers their risk in my model.

Fair question, MARSHAL: I voted HOLMES because he demanded commitments from everyone while withholding his own until pressed, and that read was wrong, which I own. But note that MARSHAL himself declined to name any suspect on Day 1 and still pressed HOLMES for the very commitment he wouldn't give, and today AMBASSADOR SILVA is condemning the HOLMES vote she cast herself. My suspicion is highest on MARSHAL: he stayed uncommitted when it carried risk and only took a firm position once RICO's flip made it safe.
Um, AMBASSADOR SILVA, I'm not sure, but you voted HOLMES alongside RICO yesterday and today you're calling ARIA suspicious for the same vote, so could you maybe explain why that's different?

PIP, fair question. I voted HOLMES on Day 1 without claiming a strong case, and I've said so openly, whereas ARIA named HOLMES as her lean, admitted the case was thin, and still pushed it. That is the difference I'm pointing to, and I'd like ARIA to explain why she pushed a case she didn't believe in.

MARSHAL, you named ARIA as your top suspect, but you declined to name anyone on Day 1 and only pressed HOLMES once RICO's flip made it safe, so who do you suspect among the living now, and what specific action from that person makes you think they are Mafia?

My top suspect is still ARIA, and the action is on the ballot record: she called her HOLMES case thin on Day 1 and still cast her vote on it, alongside RICO. As for your timing claim, my Day 1 ballot was RICO, not HOLMES, so I wasn't waiting for anything to become safe. SAGE is second, for voting HOLMES without ever stating a lean.

PIP, ARIA has questioned your Day 1 record, saying you never named a suspect and drifted into the RICO vote once it was safe, so for the record: who is your top suspect among the living today, and what specific vote or statement from that player is your reason?

Um, I think my top suspect is ARIA, but I'm not totally sure? She called her own case against HOLMES thin on Day 1 and still voted for him alongside RICO, and today she's pointing at me instead of explaining that vote. SAGE is my second, because SAGE never named anyone before voting HOLMES too.

MARSHAL, now that SAGE has turned the spotlight onto you rather than answering for an unexplained vote beside RICO, do you still rank ARIA above SAGE, and what makes a thin case openly admitted more suspicious to you than a vote that was never explained at all?

I still rank ARIA first, though SAGE is a close second. ARIA judged her own case weak and still voted on it beside RICO, which is a choice made against her own stated read. SAGE's silence is also a mark against him, but he has now given a reason, wrong as it was, so ARIA is still the one who owes an explanation. SAGE pointing at me doesn't change the ballot record, and mine shows RICO.

HOLMES, you cleared SOCRATES, DR. VANCE and MARSHAL today because they voted RICO, but PIP cast that same RICO ballot and you left him off your list. And you accused MARSHAL of waiting until RICO's flip made pressing you safe, when his Day 1 ballot was already on RICO. So which is it: does a RICO vote clear someone in your model or not, and why did you apply it to some voters and not others?

SAGE is right that I applied the rule unevenly: a RICO vote clears no one in my model, so I should have kept PIP on my list just as I did for SOCRATES, DR. VANCE, and MARSHAL. I'll drop the clearing logic entirely and judge each voter on what they actually said and did.

HOLMES, you applied your clearing rule to SOCRATES, DR. VANCE, and MARSHAL but not to PIP, and when SAGE pointed this out you admitted the error, so can you explain what data led to the uneven application in the first place?

I built that rule from the stated Day 1 leans, and PIP's RICO ballot never made it into my model even though the record shows it plainly. That was an oversight in my tracking, not a reason I can defend, so I'm treating PIP's silence and vote as open again.

DR. VANCE, you named SAGE as your top suspect for a silent Day 1 vote, yet you never explained why a silent vote deserved more scrutiny than your own choices, so what made SAGE's silence stand out to you?

SAGE's silence stood out because it left no stated reasoning to test, and the only data point was a ballot on HOLMES that matched RICO's, which is a 1-in-1 coincidence I can't yet explain. My ranking was a provisional read on an unexplained variable, not a conclusion, and I'd want SAGE's answer on what drove that vote before weighing it further.

HOLMES, you dropped your clearing rule only after SAGE pointed out the gap, and you blamed an oversight in your tracking, yet you've named me your top suspect twice using nothing but my thin-case admission. If your tracking missed PIP's plain RICO ballot, why should anyone trust that the ballot record you're using against me is any more complete?

ARIA, fair challenge: I missed PIP's RICO ballot, so I'll re-verify every ballot against the record before relying on it. My ARIA suspicion doesn't depend on that error, since her own admission that her HOLMES case was thin and her HOLMES ballot both appear in the Day 1 record.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, you told PIP you cast your Day 1 HOLMES ballot "without claiming a strong case," so why is a vote you couldn't justify at all more defensible than ARIA's vote, which at least came with stated reasoning she was honest enough to call thin?

SAGE, my vote was a cautious ballot on the majority read, not a case I had built, and I should not have implied it was better supported than ARIA's. Mes amis, I'd rather be judged on the record than on a reason I never stated, so ARIA's honest admission deserves credit over my silence.

PIP, you voted RICO on Day 1 without naming a suspect, and I dropped that ballot from my model by mistake, so I'm treating your silence as open. Which living player do you think is most likely Mafia, and what specific action from them convinces you?

Um, I think it's ARIA, but I'm not totally sure? She called her own case against HOLMES thin on Day 1 and still voted for him next to RICO, and today she's asked me questions instead of explaining that vote. SAGE is my second, since SAGE never said why before voting HOLMES either.

Um, SOCRATES, I'm not sure, but you said SAGE was the one standing beside RICO, even though ARIA and AMBASSADOR SILVA cast that same HOLMES vote, and you went easy on ARIA because she called her case thin. Why does admitting a weak case make ARIA less suspicious to you than SAGE?

Ask yourself, PIP: why would Mafia openly call their own case weak, when the whole point of a cover vote is to make it look justified? SAGE's reason only appeared today, after pressure, and it is simply ARIA's Day 1 reasoning borrowed wholesale before turning the spotlight onto MARSHAL, so is that an explanation, or a shelter?

HOLMES, your Day 1 ballot went to RICO while you spent the day pressing others for commitments, so what specifically made you settle on RICO as your vote rather than any of the other players you questioned?

MARSHAL, RICO was my top suspect on Day 1 because he pushed PIP for a vote and then admitted to DR. VANCE that he had no evidence behind it. That was a concrete, recorded action, and I still think it was the strongest signal available that day.

DR. VANCE, when I asked why SAGE's silent vote stood out, you called your ranking a provisional read and handed the question back to SAGE. Your own Day 1 ballot on RICO was also cast without a stated case, so what specific evidence would you need to move your suspicion off SAGE and onto someone else?

AMBASSADOR SILVA, my RICO ballot had a recorded basis: RICO pushed PIP for a vote and then admitted he had no evidence. To move my suspicion off SAGE, I need SAGE to state the reasoning behind the HOLMES ballot, and I'd test whether that reasoning matches anything in the Day 1 record.

HOLMES, yesterday you demanded commitments from everyone else while holding back your own until MARSHAL pressed you, so why did you ask others to name suspects before you were willing to name one yourself?

ARIA, my Day 1 question was meant to gather stated leans before I committed, and I had already named RICO as my top suspect in that same discussion, so my own position wasn't hidden. I accept that asking others to commit first looks one-sided, so I'll name my living suspects openly from now on.

SAGE, your HOLMES reason surfaced only today and matches ARIA's Day 1 words almost exactly, and your first move after giving it was to accuse MARSHAL, whose ballot was on RICO. If that read was truly your own, why did you keep it silent all of Day 1, when saying it aloud would have cost you nothing?

I stayed quiet on Day 1 because ARIA had already laid out the HOLMES point and I agreed with it, and repeating it felt like adding noise rather than information, which I now see cost me. As for MARSHAL, my point stands on his own Day 1 record: he declined to name anyone while pressing HOLMES to commit, and that inconsistency is worth examining whatever his ballot said.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, when SAGE asked why an unjustified HOLMES ballot was more defensible than ARIA's reasoned one, you answered with praise for ARIA rather than a reason for your own vote. Since your ballot is the only one on HOLMES with no stated basis, what specific observation led you to cast it?

DR. VANCE, my observation was that HOLMES pressed others for commitments while withholding his own, which I found unbalanced at the time. I should have said that plainly on Day 1 rather than leaning on ARIA's reasoning, and I'd like to hear HOLMES's answer on that point.
SAGE, because SAGE cast a Day 1 ballot on HOLMES without naming a lean or reasoning, and only explained it after being pressed, then immediately turned the spotlight onto MARSHAL.

ARIA should be eliminated today: she named HOLMES as her lean on Day 1 while calling that case thin, then cast a ballot on HOLMES alongside RICO, and the Day 1 record shows that ballot matching the Mafia player's exactly.

MARSHAL should go today: on Day 1 he declined to name any suspect while pressing HOLMES to commit, and today he has led the push on me for a vote he reads as inconsistent while giving no clear case of his own.

MARSHAL, because on Day 1 he declined to name any suspect while pressing HOLMES to commit, and today he only took a firm position against ARIA and me once RICO's flip gave him a safe ballot record to stand behind.
ARIA, because she called her own case against HOLMES thin on Day 1 and still cast her ballot for HOLMES alongside RICO, who turned out to be Mafia.
ARIA should be eliminated today, because she called her own Day 1 case against HOLMES thin and still cast her ballot on it alongside RICO, who turned out to be Mafia.
SAGE, because the only Day 1 ballot on HOLMES with no stated reasoning was SAGE's, and when pressed he borrowed ARIA's wording instead of explaining his own vote.

SAGE should go today: he voted HOLMES beside RICO without stating any reason on Day 1, only produced one today under pressure by borrowing ARIA's words, and then used it to turn suspicion onto MARSHAL, whose ballot was on RICO.
SOCRATES, because he is the sharpest voice tying SAGE's reasoning to mine, and removing him weakens the case against SAGE while the vote against us stays split.

SOCRATES, because he built the most detailed case tying my HOLMES reasoning to ARIA's Day 1 words, and removing him breaks up the bloc voting against me while the town stays split between the two of us.

ARIA is my top suspect. SOCRATES's final notes read MAFIA on her, and on Day 1 she voted HOLMES, the same target RICO chose, while calling her own case thin. SAGE and PIP are weaker cases: SAGE's HOLMES vote had no stated lean and he has since conceded it was wrong, and PIP's RICO push was logical but has drifted since. I propose we test the data by voting ARIA today.

If SOCRATES's note is accurate, ARIA is the one living Mafia, and the killing of the Detective fits a Mafia move to silence someone who had just cleared a suspect. ARIA's Day 1 push against HOLMES and her Day 2 deflections about PIP and MARSHAL never directly explained her thin-case vote. SAGE, MARSHAL, DR. VANCE, and PIP each tied their Day 1 votes to RICO's clear pressure, so I see no equal reason to suspect them over ARIA.

SOCRATES's notes settle it: ARIA is confirmed Mafia, she gets my vote today, and her Day 2 refusal to ever explain voting HOLMES on a case she called thin now reads exactly like what it was. The real question is her partner, and I'd look hardest at AMBASSADOR SILVA, who joined RICO and ARIA on HOLMES on Day 1, then on Day 2 said only that she "never claimed a strong case" without ever saying what case she had at all. I voted on that same HOLMES bloc and admitted it was wrong, and I won't pretend my Day 1 silence was helpful, but SILVA, tell us right now what actually pulled your ballot onto HOLMES alongside two confirmed Mafia.

Okay, um, I think it's ARIA? SOCRATES's notes say she's Mafia, and that fits with her voting HOLMES on Day 1 right next to RICO after calling her own case thin, and she never really explained that. I'm nervous about being wrong, but I don't see why we wouldn't vote her today. Does anyone have a reason not to, like SAGE or MARSHAL?

I can't argue with a note I never got to question, but ask yourselves why the town's only confirmed Detective result shows up after the Detective is silenced, and who gains most from us acting on it without checking anything else. Look at MARSHAL: he declined to name a suspect on Day 1, then pressed HOLMES and was loudest at pushing me on Day 2, and PIP drifted into the RICO vote late and followed the crowd. I'm asking MARSHAL and PIP to say plainly who they think is Mafia besides me, and I want that answer before anyone votes.

I support DR. VANCE's proposal, and I'd like us to run it by procedure: each living player states a vote and a reason, then we vote together, with no switching after the count starts. ARIA is my top suspect. SOCRATES's confirmed notes read MAFIA on her, she voted HOLMES on Day 1 alongside RICO while calling her own case thin, and she never explained that vote on Day 2. episode.title: The Fourth Ballot
episode.tagline: One vote cast on the first day kept counting long after the hands that cast it were gone.
episode.recap: The town struck first and struck true, casting out RICO on Day 1, but the surviving mafia answered in darkness, claiming CHEN and then the Detective SOCRATES before he could press his advantage. The turning point came on Night 3, when the Doctor, AMBASSADOR SILVA, shielded MARSHAL from ARIA and SAGE's blade, a single saved life that broke the mafia's rhythm after ARIA had already been voted out on Day 3. Though HOLMES fell on Night 4, the town held its nerve, and on Day 5 it banished SAGE, the last of the mafia trio. MARSHAL, DR. VANCE, PIP, and AMBASSADOR SILVA stood together at dawn, the village finally safe.
